name: Golden Horde's Great Troubles, Fragmentation Begins
summary: The 'Great Troubles' (Velikaya Zamyatnya) of the Golden Horde (1360-1380) see approximately 20 khans in 20 years, assassination and civil war becoming endemic. Mamai (a non-Genghisid who controls the western portion) faces challenges from Tokhtamysh (backed by Timur) from the east. This internal chaos enables Moscow's growing military resistance, culminating in Kulikovo (1380).

_quarry.structural_significance: The Golden Horde's fragmentation is the necessary precondition for Russian independence; the tributary states (Moscow, Tver, Novgorod) can build strength during periods when Horde authority is disputed; Timur's destruction of the Horde (1396-1397) accelerates its disintegration into the successor khanates (Crimea, Kazan, Astrakhan, Siberia); Moscow's rise exploits this fragmentation systematically
